title: The River in the Sentence
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空事例。実在の史料、法律、医療助言、調査結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: In an invented poem, a speaker describes a river running past the house where she spent her childhood.
sentences.ja: 創作詩で語り手は幼少期を過ごした家のそばを流れる川を描く。

sentences.en: The poem first appears to describe a particular natural landscape, and several details suggest that the speaker remembers the place clearly.
sentences.ja: 詩は最初特定の自然景観を描くように見え、いくつかの細部は場所を明確に覚えていることを示唆する。

sentences.en: However, the river later seems to represent something that cannot physically flow past a house.
sentences.ja: しかし後にその川は物理的には家のそばを流れられないものを表すように見える。

sentences.en: The reader is invited to consider how the same image can contribute to different levels of meaning within a single work.
sentences.ja: 読者は同一のイメージが一作品内の異なる意味の層にどう貢献し得るか考えるよう促される。

sentences.en: One reader interprets the river as an image of time because the speaker repeatedly refers to things that have changed since her childhood.
sentences.ja: ある読者は語り手が幼少期から変化した物事に繰り返し言及するので川を時間のイメージと解釈する。

sentences.en: Another reader pays more attention to the fact that the water passes through several places before reaching the speaker's former home.
sentences.ja: 別の読者は水が語り手のかつての家に達する前に複数の場所を通過する事実により注意を払う。

sentences.en: For this reader, the image suggests a connection between experiences that appear to belong to different periods of life.
sentences.ja: この読者にはイメージが人生の異なる時期に属するように見える経験間のつながりを示唆する。

sentences.en: The interpretations are not necessarily incompatible, although each emphasizes a different aspect of the text.
sentences.ja: それぞれが本文の異なる側面を強調するが、解釈は必ずしも両立しないものではない。

sentences.en: A teacher asks a class to replace the river with a clock in a short section of the invented poem.
sentences.ja: 教師は創作詩の短い箇所で川を時計に置き換えるようクラスに求める。

sentences.en: The new image might preserve the association with time while weakening the sense of movement between different physical locations.
sentences.ja: 新しいイメージは時間との連想を保ちつつ異なる物理的位置間の移動感を弱めるかもしれない。

sentences.en: Students compare the original and modified versions in order to identify what has been gained and what has been lost through the substitution.
sentences.ja: 生徒は置換で得られたものと失われたものを特定するため原版と変更版を比較する。

sentences.en: They recognize that identifying a possible meaning of an image does not necessarily justify replacing the image with a direct explanation.
sentences.ja: イメージの可能な意味を特定してもそれを直接説明に置き換えることが必ずしも正当化されないと認識する。

sentences.en: The class also examines whether particular descriptions in the poem support the different interpretations.
sentences.ja: 詩の特定描写が異なる解釈を支えるかも調べる。

sentences.en: A reader may discover a new association, but a convincing account of the work should explain how that association relates to its language.
sentences.ja: 読者は新たな連想を発見するかもしれないが、説得力のある作品説明はその連想が作品の言葉にどう関係するか説明するべきだ。

sentences.en: The exercise therefore encourages imagination without treating every possible interpretation as equally supported by the text.
sentences.ja: そこで活動は全可能解釈が本文に同等に支持されると扱わず想像力を促す。

sentences.en: It illustrates a way of reading a fictional poem rather than providing historical information about an actual author.
sentences.ja: 実在作家の歴史情報を提供するのでなく創作詩の読み方を例示する。

sentences.en: A literary image can preserve connections that would be difficult to express through a single abstract statement.
sentences.ja: 文学的イメージは単一抽象記述では表現しにくいつながりを保ち得る。

sentences.en: Interpreting such an image involves paying attention both to the possibilities it creates and to the details that limit those possibilities.
sentences.ja: その解釈には生じる可能性とその可能性を制限する細部の両方への注意が伴う。

sentences.en: The river in the sentence becomes more than a substitute for another word.
sentences.ja: 一文の川は別の語の代用品以上のものとなる。

sentences.en: It is part of the way the poem invites its reader to think.
sentences.ja: 詩が読者に思考を促す方法の一部なのだ。

questions.prompt: What change occurs in the apparent role of the river?
options: It disappears from every version of the poem.
It becomes a physical clock.
It proves the speaker has no memories.
It begins to suggest a meaning beyond the literal landscape.
questions.explanation_ja: 文字通りの景観を超える意味。

questions.prompt: What place is mentioned in the poem?
options: A fictional classroom full of clocks.
A house where the speaker spent her childhood.
The house of the teacher.
A city she has never visited.

questions.prompt: Why does one reader associate the river with time?
options: The speaker refers repeatedly to changes since childhood.
The poem gives the exact time of an event.
The river is described as a clock.
The reader knows the author's actual biography.

questions.prompt: Why might the two interpretations coexist?
options: They necessarily contradict each other.
Neither makes use of the image.
They emphasize different aspects of the same text.
The text establishes only one meaning explicitly.

questions.prompt: What substitution does the teacher propose?
options: Replace the speaker with a teacher.
Replace the river with a clock.
Remove every description.
Replace the poem with a historical article.
questions.explanation_ja: 川を時計に置き換える。

questions.prompt: What might be lost through that substitution?
options: Every association with time.
The ability to write a sentence.
The existence of a speaker.
The sense of movement between places.
The novelty of the interpretation alone.
Agreement with every other reader.
Connections between the proposed meaning and the language of the poem.
A claim about an author's life without evidence.

questions.prompt: What does the exercise not provide?
options: Historical information about a real author.
An example of textual interpretation.
Opportunities for imaginative reading.
A comparison of different meanings.
questions.explanation_ja: 実在作家についての史実ではない。

options: Always written in a foreign language.
Produced entirely without thought.
Physically present in a river.
Related to ideas rather than concrete objects.

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the passage?
options: Every literary image can be replaced by a single abstract word.
Readers should accept all interpretations equally.
Literary images can express multiple connected meanings that must be interpreted in relation to textual evidence.
The literal meaning of a poem is always irrelevant.
questions.explanation_ja: イメージの複数の意味と本文の根拠。

paraphrases.source: However, the river later seems to represent something that cannot physically flow past a house.

paraphrases.source: The interpretations are not necessarily incompatible, although each emphasizes a different aspect of the text.
paraphrases.rewrite: The readings may coexist despite emphasizing different textual features.

paraphrases.source: The new image might preserve the association with time while weakening the sense of movement between different physical locations.
paraphrases.rewrite: A clock may retain the idea of time but reduce the feeling of physical movement.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 置換で得るものと失うもの。

paraphrases.source: Interpreting such an image involves paying attention both to the possibilities it creates and to the details that limit those possibilities.
paraphrases.rewrite: Readers consider both the meanings an image makes possible and the textual limits on them.
